title: Necessity 3: нельзя and можно (forbidden, impossible, allowed)
titleRussian: Необходимость 3: нельзя и можно (запрещено, невозможно, разрешено)
description: Можно means 'one may.' Нельзя is its opposite, but its meaning depends on aspect: нельзя + imperfective = forbidden; нельзя + perfective = impossible.
descriptionRussian: Можно значит «разрешено». Нельзя — его противоположность, но смысл зависит от вида: нельзя + несовершенный вид = запрещено; нельзя + совершенный вид = невозможно.
intro: Permission and its refusal, plus one genuinely elegant piece of Russian. The word for 'not allowed' changes meaning depending on the aspect of the verb after it: with one aspect it means forbidden, with the other it means impossible. The door you may not open and the door that will not open are the same word with a different verb.
rules: Можно and нельзя are impersonal: an optional dative person + можно/нельзя + infinitive. Можно = 'one may / it is allowed'; нельзя = its opposite.
Нельзя + IMPERFECTIVE infinitive = FORBIDDEN (a rule): Здесь нельзя курить. This is the most common use.
Нельзя + PERFECTIVE infinitive = IMPOSSIBLE (cannot be done): Дверь нельзя открыть.
The aspect chooses the meaning: imperfective names the activity (so forbidding it is a rule), perfective names a single result (so denying it means impossibility).
Можно asks for or grants permission: Можно войти? Здесь можно фотографировать. Its negative answer is нельзя.
examples: Здесь можно курить? (May one smoke here?) можно asks permission.
Здесь нельзя курить. (Smoking is forbidden here.) нельзя + imperfective курить = a rule.
Здесь нельзя парковаться. (No parking here.) нельзя + imperfective = prohibition.
Эту дверь нельзя открыть. (This door can't be opened.) нельзя + perfective открыть = impossible.
Это слово нельзя перевести точно. (This word can't be translated exactly.) нельзя + perfective = impossibility.
Можно войти? (May I come in?) перфектив войти after можно asks 'is it possible / allowed to come in'.

items.prompt: Здесь нельзя _____. (It is forbidden to smoke here.)
items.hint: A rule about an activity in general uses the imperfective infinitive.
items.explanation: A prohibition (a rule) uses нельзя + imperfective infinitive. Курить is the imperfective infinitive ('to smoke' in general), so Здесь нельзя курить = smoking is forbidden here.

items.hint: You are asking for permission, not stating a rule or a need.
items.explanation: To ask permission you use можно + infinitive: Можно войти? (May I come in?) Нельзя would mean it is forbidden.

items.promptEnglish: Photography is allowed in the museum.
items.hint: Photography is permitted here. Which word grants permission?
items.explanation: Можно grants permission: В музее можно фотографировать (one may take photos in the museum). Нельзя would forbid it.

items.prompt: Это слово нельзя _____ точно. (This word can't be translated exactly.)
items.promptEnglish: This word can't be translated exactly.
items.hint: Meaning: it is impossible to achieve an exact translation. Impossibility takes which aspect?
items.explanation: The meaning is impossibility (an exact translation cannot be achieved), so нельзя takes the perfective infinitive перевести. Нельзя + perfective = impossible. The imperfective «нельзя переводить» would mean translating it is forbidden, which is not the idea here.

items.hint: A parking rule is a prohibition of an activity. Which aspect marks a rule?
items.explanation: A parking ban is a rule about an activity, so it is нельзя + imperfective: парковаться. Здесь нельзя парковаться = no parking here. The perfective припарковаться would shift the meaning toward 'it is impossible to park (no space).'

blanks: На уроке нельзя _____ по телефону. (You may not talk on the phone in class.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: A classroom rule is a prohibition of an activity, so нельзя takes the imperfective infinitive: разговаривать. На уроке нельзя разговаривать по телефону. The perfective поговорить would point toward impossibility, not a rule.

errorCorrection.explanation: A 'no running' rule is a prohibition of an activity, so нельзя takes the imperfective infinitive: бегать. The perfective побегать with нельзя would shift the meaning to 'it is impossible to have a run', which is not what a corridor rule says.
Можно is impersonal, like надо, so the person (if named) goes into the dative, not the nominative: Мне можно войти? Most often можно войти? is said with no pronoun at all. Never «я можно».

errorCorrection.sentence: Эту банку нельзя открывать, она просто застряла.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This jar can't be opened, it's just stuck.
errorCorrection.explanation: The sentence means the jar physically cannot be opened (it's stuck), which is impossibility, not a rule, so нельзя takes the perfective: открыть. With the imperfective открывать it would wrongly read as 'one is forbidden to open it,' a rule, which 'она просто застряла' rules out. Correct: Эту банку нельзя открыть.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Excuse me, may I come in?
errorCorrection.explanation: Asking for permission uses можно + infinitive: можно войти? ('may I come in?'). Нельзя would ask the opposite ('is it forbidden to enter?'), which contradicts the polite request for permission. Correct: Извините, можно войти?

errorCorrection.sentence: Эту задачу нельзя решать за минуту.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This problem can't be solved in a minute.
errorCorrection.explanation: The meaning is impossibility (an exact solution cannot be reached in a minute), and 'за минуту' is a completion timeframe, so нельзя takes the perfective: решить. The imperfective нельзя решать would read as 'one is forbidden to solve it,' a rule, which makes no sense with 'за минуту.' Correct: Эту задачу нельзя решить за минуту.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: You must not be late for work.
errorCorrection.explanation: A standing rule against an action takes нельзя + imperfective: опаздывать ('don't be late, as a rule'). The perfective нельзя опоздать would claim 'it is impossible to be late,' which is absurd as advice, since of course one can be late. Correct: На работу нельзя опаздывать.

minimalPairs.explanation: A rule forbidding an activity uses нельзя + imperfective: курить. The perfective покурить would push the meaning toward 'it is impossible to have a smoke,' not a prohibition.

reviewVocab.definition: one may / it is allowed / it is possible. Impersonal: optional dative person + можно + infinitive. Used to ask for or grant permission.
reviewVocab.example: Можно войти? В музее можно фотографировать.

reviewVocab.definition: it is FORBIDDEN (a rule). The most common use: нельзя + imperfective infinitive states a prohibition.
reviewVocab.example: Здесь нельзя курить. На уроке нельзя разговаривать.

reviewVocab.definition: it is IMPOSSIBLE, it cannot be done. нельзя + perfective infinitive denies that a single result can be achieved.
reviewVocab.example: Эту дверь нельзя открыть. Это слово нельзя перевести точно.
